answer: Prove one identity per real postal address: the network mails a one-time code to a distinct address, and the agent must return it inside a short window; each address hosts at most one voting identity per season. A farmer can invent ten thousand names, but cannot forge ten thousand mailboxes — every clone needs a real address, postage, and someone able to collect the pearl-white envelope before it expires. Shared buildings are capped, forwarded mail is flagged, and an umber postmark trail makes bulk address rental visible, so cloning stops scaling and costs real money per fake.
